name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (verb 'apply' + descriptor 'palette_remap_run'). Accurately reflects body: applies a 256-byte translation LUT over a contiguous run of bytes in place. No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix matching its own address or any data address). 'run' correctly denotes the contiguous byte-span semantics, matching the do-while-over-byte_count loop.
purpose: In-place 8-bit byte remap over a contiguous run: for byte_count bytes at buf, replaces each byte b with remap_table[b] (a 256-entry translation LUT). Used by the filled-circle/AoE band animators to recolor a horizontal pixel run of the off-screen render buffer under a circular spell/warp effect.
logic_summary: EAX is zeroed, then a do-while LOOP (counter=byte_count): LODSB loads the current source byte (zero-extended into EAX), MOV AL,[EAX+EDX] looks it up in remap_table, STOSB writes it back. ESI (read) and EDI (write) start at the same address (buf) and advance in lockstep, so the lookup result overwrites the same byte just read -> a true in-place remap. LOOP decrements byte_count and repeats while non-zero. No zero-check: byte_count==0 underflows ECX to run 2^32 times, so callers must pass count >= 1. void return.
signature: void fd2_apply_palette_remap_run(uint32 remap_table, uint32 byte_count, uint8 *buf)

params.name: remap_table
params.semantics: Base address of a 256-byte translation LUT; each source byte value b indexes remap_table[b] to get the replacement byte. Passed by callers as a palette-remap source row pointer.
params.reason: Accurately names the LUT base; no address residue; matches body use as the base of an indexed byte lookup (MOV AL,[EAX+EDX]).

params.name: byte_count
params.semantics: Number of bytes to process; serves as the LOOP counter (ECX). Callers pass the clamped horizontal pixel-run width. Must be >= 1 (do-while, no zero-check).
params.reason: Accurately names the iteration count; no address residue; matches the LOOP-counter role.

params.name: buf
params.semantics: In-place buffer pointer: the contiguous byte run that is both read and written. Callers pass a horizontal pixel run inside the off-screen render buffer (_large_game_state_buffer + 0x8088 + row*0x1C8 + left_clip).
params.reason: Conventional and accurate for the in-place buffer; no address residue; both ESI (LODSB) and EDI (STOSB) operate on this same span.

returns.semantics: No return value; the only effect is the in-place remap of the byte run at buf.

comment_original_issue: Plate's 'Used for' line listed speculative use cases (select-cursor color cycling, dimmed-sprite transformation, status-flash recolor) that do not match the two verified callers. The src comment was accurate but generic (no usage context).
notes: Decompiler split buf into two SSA pointers (dst_iter for STOSB write, buf for LODSB read) and printed the read as *(undefined1*)((uint)*buf + remap_table); disassembly @ 0x4DB9C confirms ESI=EDI=buf advancing in lockstep, so it is a genuine in-place remap (buf[i] = remap_table[buf[i]]) -- not a logic concern, just a decompiler artifact. No globals read/written by this function (all three operands are stack params). Verified callers: fd2_render_circle_anim_row @ 0x219AD, fd2_render_filled_circle_band_anim @ 0x22046, both passing remap_table=palette-remap source pointer, byte_count=clamped run width, buf=render-buffer pixel-run pointer. src comment augmented (palette.c lines 241-261) to add the verified caller/usage context; Ghidra plate updated to replace the speculative use-case list with the verified callers while preserving its detailed body/algorithm description. Name and all three params kept (convention-compliant, no address residue).
